clauses.reason: The sole operative sentence of Executive Order 8304 revokes Executive Order No. 2552 of March 21, 1917, which withdrew public land in Alaska for lighthouse purposes; its operative words are 'is hereby revoked'. A present-tense revocation with no later effective date is carried out when the order takes effect, so the command was exhausted by performance on the order's signing date, 1939-12-19, which is recorded as the end. The filing date December 20, 1939 and the issue date December 22, 1939 are the alternatives if effectiveness is dated from filing or publication. The Federal Register docket line reads 'Filed, December 20, 1939;' and the issue is headed 'Washington, Friday, December 22, 1939'.

research_rationale:
Identity and text: the held original is the machine-extracted text layer of the official Federal Register issue (4 FR 4909, PDF pages 1-1, https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-1939-12-22/pdf/FR-1939-12-22.pdf, sha256 219867f10645ab4bfd1ade1aec42fbd1234152da7b31967961625065186d7f4d); the text layer is OCR, the page image is not held in the repository, and the order was identified from the text layer. The order's heading, subject, signature date and closing number tag appear together as one short order whose whole text is the clause. Inventory: one operative sentence revoking Executive Order No. 2552 of March 21, 1917, which withdrew public land in Alaska for lighthouse purposes; there is no other clause. End: a present-tense revocation is carried out when the order takes effect, and the order postpones nothing, so the command was exhausted by performance on its signing date 1939-12-19; the filing date December 20, 1939 and the issue date December 22, 1939 are the alternative dates if effectiveness is dated from filing or publication. The packet's one machine lead for a later instrument is Executive Order 10287 of September 6, 1951. Its held heading cites the number 8304 with the date January 14, 1939, which does not match this order (signed December 19, 1939), and its body revokes a different order, number 8034 of January 14, 1939, and abolishes the Federal Real Estate Board. It does not revoke or name this order and is rejected as a lead. Later instruments: the packet's later-events search of Office of the Federal Register disposition notes (1937 onward) and its current-law searches of the U.S. Code and the eCFR were selected after reading their coverage notes, and each returned no hit for this order. A later revocation or repeal of the order is not needed to end a command that was already performed.

savings.reason: The held text contains no savings or transition clause. Its single command, revocation of Executive Order No. 2552 of March 21, 1917, which withdrew public land in Alaska for lighthouse purposes, was completed when the order took effect. The revoked order's loss of effect is a completed consequence that survives as an accrued result, not as a continuing command of this order.
